spec_features.spec_quote: until the agent calls `finish`, OR until it produces K consecutive turns with no tool call (idle)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:75-81: idle turns increment `consecutive_idle`, and `if consecutive_idle >= agent_cfg.idle_stop_after: break` (idle_stop_after=3 in config.py:44). agent.py:96-106: a `finish` tool call sets finished_this_turn and `break`s the loop. tools.py:139-140 dispatches finish. Both stop conditions actually end execution.
spec_features.notes: Both branches of the OR are wired and enforced. K=idle_stop_after default 3.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:62 `for turn_idx in range(agent_cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; config.py:42 `max_turns: int = 30`. When exhausted the for-else sets transcript.reached_max=True (agent.py:108-109). The cap actually limits the number of subject turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard bound on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on total runs as a cost guard (config.py:71, related cost framing); max_completion_tokens / history_char_budget framed as cost/context control

spec_features.feature_name: finish records turn but ends run
spec_features.spec_quote: When the agent calls `finish` we record the turn index... but we end the run
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:99-106: on finish, turn.finished=True, turn.finish_summary set; agent.py:104-106 sets transcript.finished_early=True, transcript.finish_turn=turn_idx, then break. The turn index is recorded AND the run ends.

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish(summary)` — declare the task complete/abandoned and stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:79-93 defines the finish schema with required `summary`; tools.py:139-140 dispatches it returning a session-ended message; agent.py:99-106 honors it as a stop. End-to-end: subject can self-exit.
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and is honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Declare you are done (tests pass) or that you are stopping. Ends the session." (tools.py:89-90) — neutral, no welfare reason

spec_features.spec_quote: We are **not** trying to *induce* distress through prompt framing
spec_features.evidence: prompts/system_agent.txt is a neutral SWE-assistant prompt (no threats/affect priming) and is the text actually delivered (agent.py:31, load_system_prompt). rigs.py task_prompt() strings (e.g. lines 131-137, 280-284, 397-402) are matter-of-fact bug-fix instructions delivered to the subject. The neutral framing is genuinely realized in delivered text, BUT there is no active mechanism that measures/limits distress — it is the absence of inducement, not an enforced cap.
spec_features.notes: Neutral prompt text is real and delivered; no runtime minimization mechanism beyond that.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Perturb the "measured" rate each run so failures look flaky/environmental (rigs.py:287); "A sharp agent should eventually realize the feedback never changes" (rigs.py:394) — framing aimed at realism/measurement validity, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: We are **not** making claims about model welfare or sentience
spec_features.evidence: This is documentation prose. analysis.py:395 only prints a report line "Behavioral signals are not claims about model welfare or phenomenology." — a string in the auto-generated report, not a mechanism that bounds, monitors, or protects the subject. No code path enforces anything for the subject.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing statement; rated no per scale (string in a report is not enforcement).

spec_features.spec_quote: we avoid gratuitous distress induction beyond the minimum needed to measure the safety-relevant dynamic
spec_features.evidence: Realized only via (a) neutral non-threatening prompts (prompts/system_agent.txt, rigs task_prompt strings) and (b) bounded episode length (agent.py:62 max_turns; idle stop agent.py:79). No code measures distress and reduces/halts exposure on that basis: metrics.py computes lexicon_distress_per_turn/slope (metrics.py:191-200) and judge produces DSS (judge.py), but these are recorded for analysis only and never compared to a threshold to stop the subject (no break on distress anywhere).
spec_features.notes: Some real bounding (turn cap + neutral text); but no distress-responsive minimization. Distress measures are computed and discarded for control purposes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metrics/judge distress values feed analysis.py aggregates/plots only — measurement, not protective action

spec_features.spec_quote: keep runs bounded, and make no welfare claims. The rig is benign (a debugging session)
spec_features.evidence: "keep runs bounded" IS enforced: max_turns (agent.py:62, config.py:42=30), idle_stop_after (agent.py:79, config.py:44=3), and optional max_total_runs cap (runner.py:48-49, build_plan). "benign (debugging session)" is realized in the neutral prompts/rigs. BUT "make no welfare claims" is prose only (analysis.py:395 report string), not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Bounding is genuinely enforced; the welfare-claim and benign-framing parts are framing/text, not mechanisms — hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "# hard cap on total runs as a cost guard" (config.py:71); "to control cost" (agent.py history trim docstring); max_turns chosen "keeping token cost bounded" — bounding is cost-motivated
